title: Rows Into Named Columns
statement:
A table library stores data column by column. You get a list of column names headers and a list of rows, where every row has one value per header, in header order. Values may be numbers or strings.

Return an object that maps each header to the list of values in its column, top to bottom. Every header must be present, even when there are no rows (its list is then empty).

This is what building a data frame from a list of records does. The original task is written for a data-frame library; here the result is a plain object so it can be checked in any language.

examples.why: Value j of each row goes to column j. The row order is kept.
No rows, but the columns still exist. Transposing with zip(*rows) in Python would lose them.

constraints: every row has exactly headers.length values
hints: The output is the input matrix turned on its side: row i, column j becomes column j, position i.
Create the empty list for every header first, so empty input still has all the keys.
Then walk the rows once and push value j into the list for headers[j].

explain.intuition:
Row-oriented data (an array of records, like a JSON API response) and column-oriented data (one array per field, like a data frame or a chart series) hold the same values. Converting between them is a transpose: the value at row i, column j moves to column j, position i.

The only trap is the empty table. If you derive the columns from the rows, zero rows give zero columns. Derive them from headers instead, and the shape is right even with no data.
steps: For each row, for each index j, push row[j] onto out[headers[j]].
pitfalls: Using zip(*rows) in Python or rows[0].map(…) in JavaScript to transpose. Both break when rows is empty.
Building rows of objects ([{id: 7, age: 21}, …]) instead of columns.
Sharing one list between all headers, for example with dict.fromkeys(headers, []), so every column receives every value.

solutions.title: One pass over the rows
solutions.idea: Start every column empty, then push each row's values into their columns.

solutions.title: Column by column
solutions.idea: For each header index j, collect row[j] from every row.

followups: Go the other way: turn the column object back into a list of row objects. What should happen if the columns have different lengths?
Rows may now be objects with missing keys. Fill missing cells with null. How do you collect the set of headers?
